programme.title: The Stuarts
programme.desc: This three-part series argues that the Stuarts, more than any other, were Britain's defining royal family. After Charles I's disastrous attempt to militarily impose political and religious uniformity throughout his kingdoms, both the Stuart dynasty and its three kingdoms fell into an abyss. Charles lost his head and his family fled into exile. In this second episode, Dr Clare Jackson reveals how the unprecedented religious violence of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms shaped the very DNA of British political culture and how the trauma suffered influenced constitutional crises in the years to come.

programme.title: Chauvet: Humanity's First Great Masterpiece
programme.desc: In December 1994, an archaeological marvel hidden deep inside France’s Gorges de l’Ardèche was revealed to the modern world for the very first time: the Chauvet cave. Scientists immediately recognised the importance of this discovery. Sealed by a landslide more than 20,000 years ago, the cave had been extraordinarily well preserved. With over 1,000 paintings adorning its walls, Chauvet is a cave art jewel. How were the hidden chambers first formed? Who created the extraordinary art? And how can we preserve it for future generations? This film follows a 30-year archaeological, geological and artistic adventure as scientists endeavour to understand and conserve this exceptional record of humanity’s distant past.

programme.title: My Week with Marilyn
programme.desc: It is 1956, and The Prince and the Showgirl is being made at Pinewood Studios in London, directed by and starring Laurence Olivier, who has recruited one of the biggest Hollywood stars of all time, Marilyn Monroe, to co-star with him. Colin Clark, a junior assistant on the production, is assigned the job of looking after Marilyn and keeps a journal about the week he spent with her. It proves to be a turbulent experience as Marilyn is going through marital problems with her husband and uses Colin as a much-needed sounding board for all her pent-up neurosis. Acclaimed drama from BBC Films based on Clark's real-life diaries.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Marilyn Monroe was, and perhaps will always be, Hollywood’s biggest female film icon and the sexiest of cinema's sex symbols, lighting up the screen in several cinema classics – including one of cinema’s greatest comedies, Some Like It Hot. The aura surrounding her has been enhanced by a sense of mystery that comes from the fact she was very rarely interviewed. But anyone who knew or worked with her was guaranteed to be asked about their personal 'Marilyn moments'. Here we tell Marilyn's story through the insights and anecdotes of friends, directors and fellow actors who spoke about her over the years on a selection of BBC programmes. With archive interviews featuring stars like Jane Russell, Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis, as well as directors like Billy Wilder and John Huston, and Marilyn's former husband Arthur Miller, these conversations paint a picture of a star who conquered Hollywood despite serious battles with her inner demons, and reveal what it was like for those who got to enter into the orbit of one of cinema's greatest stars.

programme.title: Eve and Marilyn
programme.desc: 'She had a total understanding and control of the still camera... she was intelligent enough and sharp enough and beautiful enough to be able to manipulate almost any situation, so it became something which was totally her own...' Eve Arnold, one of the world's leading photo-journalists, remembers photographing Marilyn Monroe over the ten crucial years of Marilyn's stardom and decline. Going back to the original contact sheets and colour material, she tells of their friendship and what it was like as a woman to photograph Marilyn Monroe.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: The AI industry has just had the fright of its life. After a shock US midterm election result handed Democrats control of both houses of Congress, the companies leading the AI revolution suddenly face an uncomfortable reality: investigations, subpoenas, public backlash and the prospect of sweeping new regulation. At the very centre of the storm is Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company sits at the heart of the global AI boom. Recent revelations surrounding Huang have triggered a crisis of confidence, wiped hundreds of billions from Nvidia's market value, and raised difficult questions about corporate governance, national security and the concentration of power inside the AI industry. Meanwhile, Elon Musk's political gamble appears to have backfired spectacularly. After pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into the midterms, Silicon Valley's most influential figures are now confronting a Congress that may be far less willing to give them the benefit of the doubt.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A speeding driver tears down a Rhyl street, wrecking cars and nearly killing a bystander pumping up his tyres. With no dashcam recording, crucial evidence comes from an unexpected source. An angry motorist takes a roundabout the wrong way to pursue another driver, while on the M4 near Newport, a lorry smashes into a car along the carriageway. A friend's dashcam holds the key to who's to blame.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion and Martel are criss-crossing the country in Bolsover, Dawley and Darlington, looking at three ambitious property projects ripe for renovation or conversion. The former working men's club, a cottage with a magnificent garden and a three-bedroom semi-detached were all sold at auction, and the three sets of buyers all have to overcome unforeseen issues to get their projects over the line.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: It’s up, up and away for an aeronautical edition of the show from Nottinghamshire. In Newark, Danny Sebastian visits a local college that saved a former passenger jet from the scrapheap and transformed it into a classroom for youngsters training to work in the air industry. Hoping to land a few deals of their own are Mel and Jodie on the red team, and Anne and Olivia on the blue team. At a misty antiques fair at Newark Showground, they dash around the stalls in search of three items they hope will sell for a profit at auction in Nottingham. First to spot a potential purchase is Jodie, but her expert Izzie Balmer isn’t mincing her words when it comes to saying no. The blues are thinking about ceramics, with a 1970s plate featuring yachts, but given the hefty price tag, the team decide not to sail away with it. Auctioneer Hettie Jago is wielding her gavel, but which team will come out on top?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team are joined in the hub by ethical hacker Jim Browning as they focus on a scammer who seems to be from the UK. He runs recovery scams, supposedly helping individuals recover lost funds, only to extort them for more money. With Jim’s help, the team work out that the British scammer, who is truly cruel to his victims, is working from an apartment block in Tbilisi, Georgia. With so much information on the scammer, can it help them to stop him defrauding a man at home in the UK?

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Cheryl turns doorbell detective when she discovers a dodgy duo taking her kid’s bike from her garden, but with the help of other victims, do they manage to crack the case? Former police inspector Anton Sullivan dons a flat cap as he heads to the countryside to highlight rural crime. And James loses his patience as his cameras capture numerous fly-tippers, so he eventually decides to confront them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams heads for the glorious Peak District, helping a Canadian couple spend up to £475,000 on a new home for them and their dog, Verona. The mystery house delivers jaw-dropping views, and Briony meets some park rangers who keep this stunning landscape in tip-top shape, including octogenarian Margaret who still volunteers on the hills.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In Ayrshire, a window signed by the poet Robert Burns and a life-changing historic Scottish canoe are both lovingly repaired by the team.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – Michelle, Tom, Megan, Ian and Beth – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Will it be game, set and match for Ben Cooper’s or Kate Bliss’s team on this episode? In Box, near Bath, presenter Caroline Hawley visits the UK’s only tennis ball manufacturer, where she learns about the origins of the tennis ball and how it gets its all-important bounce! Hoping to ace it at the fair are friends Helen and Marsha on the red team. Their opponents in blue are pals Clark and Michele, who are in it ‘for gavels and fame’. With 60 minutes on the clock, they take a shine to a Georgian-style silver serving dish – but not the three-figure price tag! The reds’ first stop is a striking pair of arts and crafts copper candlesticks, but the cost quickly snuffs out their interest in them. At Tim Weeks’s auction in Wiltshire, the bidders snap up the teams’ items. Will it come down to a battle of the bonus buys?

programme.desc: The cryptocurrency scammers based in Albania are back at it as the team listen in. programme.desc: A van pulls across a motorcyclist’s path near Wrexham, sending him over the handlebars and through its windscreen. His helmet camera survives, recording vital evidence. An insurer untangles a messy roundabout crash, while cyclists film a driver glued to a phone and a car cutting straight across a mini-roundabout. Another driver jumps a queue and a red light, nearly flattening a cyclist.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles visits Nottingham’s Gothic revival cathedral to learn how conservators are revealing 19th-century artwork under decades of plaster and paint. Designed in 1842 by architect Augustus Pugin, the cathedral’s interior was whitewashed in the 1960s. Pugin is widely admired for his work on some of Britain’s most famous buildings, including the Palace of Westminster. Conservator Ana Logreira shows Eric how they are using digitally created stencils to renovate the cathedral’s historic interior. At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, red team uncle and niece Russ and Lily are up against twin sisters Angie and Tamsin in blue. With just 60 minutes to buy three items, Russ makes an early pit stop at a stall selling boxed toy cars. Meanwhile, a marcasite brooch catches the sisters’ attention, but expert Irita Marriott isn’t convinced it will dazzle the bidders. Trying to hammer out a profit for the teams in Nottingham is auctioneer Hettie Jago, who has her eye on the jewellery among the lots.

programme.title: BBC News at One

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: The worlds of windsurfing and funeral directing collide when a body is found washed up on the beach. With Joe along for the ride, Rose and Raj must find what connects them.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations of the same family need help from Jules Hudson to find them a new, rural Norfolk home. In the kitty is £800,000 for a four-bedroom house, an annexe for Granny and enough land for a Shetland pony. Jules also needs a keen eye to spot some of the world’s rarest (and camera-shy) species of deer and antelope at a local safari park.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero. York Minster is one of our most magnificent cathedrals, boasting the world’s largest expanse of medieval stained glass. But the stonework of this glorious gothic monument is crumbling away on a daily basis. Will and Dom join the new generation of stonemasons being trained to save it, harnessing modern technology while still using centuries-old skills. Will’s Yorkshire odyssey continues in Cawthorne, where Elwin presents him with a huge drum that has been owned by the local marching band since the 1850s. The damaged paintwork, ill-fitting skins and loose cords aren’t befitting such a magnificent instrument, so percussion expert Pete Woods takes on the mammoth task of getting it back into a playable condition. Dom heads further south through God’s Own Country to visit occasional Repair Shop expert Jonathan Reid in his Sheffield workshop. Here the master putter, or scissor-maker, is keeping the endangered craft of making scissors by hand alive, and he’s eager to share some secrets of the trade with his fellow craftsman.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – William, Nicky, Abz, Chris and Charlotte – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Return to Paradise
programme.desc: Lights, camera, murder. The anniversary screening of Dolphin Cove cult horror film Blood Wave goes off with a literal bang when one of its key creatives is killed during the iconic gunshot sequence. But how did the killer fire the gun in front of the packed house without the audience realising? Theories abound, and not just about the murder, as Colin questions what significance the film holds for Mack and Glenn. And as the case builds to its climax, Mackenzie doesn't know whether it's harder to solve the crime or give Leo an answer when he asks her out on a date.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show
programme.desc: Together on Graham's sofa are Hollywood legend Robert De Niro and comedy great Ben Stiller, reunited in Focker-in-Law; Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh, talking about her new TV series Bladerunner 2099; and top chef Jamie Oliver, whose latest book is 20-Minute Meals. With music from Take That, performing their current single, Higher.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: As police piece together the last few minutes of Cimarron’s life, they realise McCartney was still online threatening her when she tragically shot herself. Police and prosecutors move quickly to establish if there’s a case for manslaughter. Police from Northern Ireland travel to West Virginia to conduct the manslaughter investigation, where they learn that Cimarron’s own family had no idea why she took her own life. In a tragic turn, they learn that 18 months after her death, Cimarron’s father had also died by suicide. In order to charge McCartney with manslaughter, the police have to prove that he foresaw the risk to her life. As they comb through the cyber evidence from his devices, they build a case for manslaughter and charge him. The case sets new legal precedent in the UK. More than five years after the police investigation began, McCartney is finally convicted and sentenced.

programme.title: Men of the Manosphere
programme.desc: James Blake joins three young men to explore why they’ve turned to the so-called manosphere to achieve success, and how it’s influenced their real lives.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May attempt to prove that cars can be art by taking over an entire modern art gallery in Middlesbrough and filling it with motoring-related works, including some remarkable creations of their own. In their quest to prove that cars can be more popular than traditional art, the presenters set themselves the challenge of attracting more visitors to their exhibition than will visit a more traditional gallery over the same period, a task that forces them to engage in some unusual promotional activities. Also on the show, Jeremy is on the test track in a new British supercar, the sensationally fast and expensive Noble M600.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson makes a film about the BMW X6 and ends up conducting one of the most expensive road tests in Top Gear history. James May drives a Vauxhall Insignia VXR, accompanied by Margaret Calvert, the designer of Britain's road signs, and Richard Hammond tests the £340,000 Lexus supercar on the Top Gear track. The boys then try out the latest in electric personal transport in the studio, and the Star in a Reasonably Priced Car is blues musician Seasick Steve.

programme.desc: In October 1996, it was full steam ahead for the Tartan Army on the way to the World Cup in France. However, when Scotland lined up to face Estonia in Tallinn, there was just one thing missing - the opposition.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Cardiff-based hopeless romantic Lewis just can’t help hearing wedding bells and talking through future life plans on date one, but that’s not the only obstacle to him getting a second date. If he’s not ranting about his exes, he’s zoning out mid-conversation, leaving his dates lost for words and never calling them again. Tired of listening to yet another of his first-date failures, Lewis’s best mate Megan thinks it’s time for an intervention, so she enlists the help one of Gen Z’s sassiest sex and relationships experts, Oloni, to drop some hard home truths on 20-year-old Lewis to try to end the bad habits that send his dates running for the hills. Oloni gives Lewis a reality check as his friends and exes tell it how it is via video feedback, explaining where it’s all going wrong. Oloni and Megan watch on as Lewis goes on a series of first dates that will challenge him to rethink his dating behaviour and become a better dater. Can Lewis ditch the wedding planning, stop raking up stories about his exes and focus on the conversation long enough to prove he can be a good date?

programme.title: Movies with Ali Plumb
programme.desc: BBC Radio 1 film critic Ali Plumb explores the UK’s most iconic and unexpected film locations. Ali provides film lovers with a guide to this film location nation, stepping into the scenes themselves to bring the magic to life, In this episode, Ali travels through the silver screen sights of Liverpool.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Sports mockumentary about GB Paralympian Darren Silverstone, who stole the hearts of a nation before his infamous chokey-o in Tokyo. For the first time, he tells his story - and starts his glorious comeback. In Tokyo 2020, Darren Silverstone was the Paras GB poster boy. (He was on yoghurts, too.) He cruised to the final and charmed the nation along the way with his signature dance move, the dazzle. But as he took that final bend ready to take gold, Silverstone lost his head and celebrated too soon - and in the process, became a national figure of fun. His subsequent journey in the public eye brought approval and consternation in equal measure: from those unforgettably self-deprecating betting adverts to his turn on The Masked Singer as Breadbin. Darren’s best friend and pilot rider in Tokyo, little Paul Potter, was never seen again in the public eye. The two haven’t spoken since. And now, Silverstone’s back. Ready to take to the tandem at Paris 2024. But is he ready? Who will he be riding with? This is I Am Darren.

programme.title: Nativity!
programme.desc: Paul Maddens is charged with the biggest challenge of his life - mounting his primary school's musical version of the Nativity. Competing against the posh neighbouring school for the honour of the best-reviewed show in town, the stakes are raised when Paul idly boasts that his ex-girlfriend Jennifer, a Hollywood producer, is coming to see his show with a view to turning it into a film. The only trouble is - they haven't spoken in years... Comedy from BBC Films.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: A wealthy shipping magnate is found dead at a Christmas party. Things get stranger when a man in London receives a mysterious Christmas card connected to the victim’s death.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Christmas is just around the corner, and Agnes already has her tinsel in a twist. Rory is getting plastic surgery, Cathy is hiding something, and the family insist upon a cost-cutting secret Santa! To make matters worse, Winnie drops a Christmas bombshell. Maybe her unusual new Christmas tree will bring Agnes some festive cheer?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown is determined to have a safe and peaceful Christmas at home this year. But with Mark and Betty rowing over the reappearance of his first love Bubbles, carol singers haunting Agnes's every waking hour and Buster installing a new Christmas tree with a very unusual feature, how will Agnes survive?

programme.title: Mindhorn
programme.desc: Has-been actor Richard Thorncroft, once the lead in popular TV detective series Mindhorn, filmed on the Isle of Man in the 80s, is called back to the island to re-enact his most famous role for a police sting. A killer is on the loose and will only speak to Mindhorn himself or he threatens to strike again.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: As Bill's 75th birthday approaches, brother Joel joins the adventure, bringing some Murray family rivalry to the golf course. Comedian Joanne McNally attempts her first ever round, while a bouncing boat trip to the Cliffs of Moher brings further unexpected encounters. Then friends and familiar faces gather to celebrate a milestone birthday – and a reflective Bill looks ahead to what might come next.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: Tammy Broskom presents a programme exploring parenting: the challenges, joys and unexpected experiences of raising children. Families come in all shapes and sizes, and throughout the programme, parents share their stories as well as the advice and the lessons they have learned along the way. Tammy is joined by Michelle Goodwin, a deaf mum, teacher and advocate for deaf families. Michelle and her wife are raising two daughters, one hearing and one deaf. They discuss their journey to parenthood, their experiences of family life and the importance of communication, making sure both children feel included and connected.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: As tensions rise between Michael and Diana, Freddie wrestles with his next steps, and the Phelans’ hunger for revenge meets Ozzie’s ultimate betrayal.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: In the second week of the heats, a fresh group of professional chefs wait in the wings of the kitchen ready to demonstrate their exceptional talent.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: Marcus and Monica are joined by special guest Alex Claridge, the chef behind The Wilderness in Birmingham, who sets the contestants the challenge of recreating a dish that demands great precision.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores wellbeing and what it means to live a healthy, balanced life. Presenter Marios Costi shares practical advice on reducing stress, finding calm and making positive changes while meeting inspiring deaf people who are breaking down barriers, building confidence and pursuing their dreams. Marios talks with Avril Langard-Tang, a senior lecturer at the University of Wolverhampton and the first deaf woman to walk solo from John O’Groats to Land’s End. She reflects on her extraordinary 980-mile journey, the physical and emotional challenges she faced and the support she received from the deaf community along the way.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. This time, it's four members of the same family, Kathryn, Rab, Francis and Jan. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Edith Bowman introduces Colin Murray to her home town of Anstruther in Fife on a food adventure. As well as its famous fish and chips, they discover how artisan bread is being made for the community. Briony May Williams bags bargains hunting for yellow stickers in the supermarket, and chef Suzie Lee reveals how Greek-style yoghurt is made in County Down. Onkar Singh Purewal discovers Swansea’s community garden produce.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Scottish coastal railway journey reaches Invergordon on the Cromarty Firth, the third great inlet on the northeast coast of the Highlands.

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Scalloper Golden Promise is pushing force-6 winds to get to newly opening scallops beds ahead of his rivals. With the boat first to the grounds, they are in for a big pay day – but only once they cover the £8,000 fuel expenses to get here. Family-owned trawler Adenia leaves Lerwick aiming to land 1,000 tonnes of mackerel in Norway in just three days' time. Shetland skipper George Anderson has 11 crew, eight of whom are family, and he is hoping the fish will meet the grade to sell into the lucrative Asian sushi market. If it does, George and the crew could be in for a million-pound pay day. Skipper Ivan Toms and 25-year-old son Rhys fish Maxine’s Pride, one of the smallest and oldest trawlers in the UK fleet. In recent years, fishing has been a struggle, with little money to reinvest in the 35-year-old boat. Fishing Cornwall’s inshore waters - reserved for smaller fishing boats - can they catch enough to give themselves a wage and put money aside for repairs?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel introduces a selection of unscreened finds from previous Roadshows. Items include an Edward VIII coronation souvenir that was hastily converted to an abdication mug.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The team are in Leicester where the 100-year-old De Montfort Hall plays host to their valuation day. Antiques experts Catherine Southon and Claire Rawle are hunting through the crowds for the finest antiques and collectables to take to auction. There are some real gems to see as they go under the hammer. Plus Paul Martin discovers that local radio was born right here in Leicester.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jake Bhardwaj, Sue Cleaver, Rachel Parris and Rav Wilding take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor has some exciting guides through all the backstage ballroom action with this week’s pro panel. Also, don’t miss an exclusive first look at how the couples are getting ready for Blackpool.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout. They navigate the area through the lens of a six-year-old Bob as he takes Paul on a trip along the landscapes of his youth. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear are of the fishing trips they used to go on. Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner. Reece has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Pain is a fact of life. For many, it is excruciating and inescapable, a truly disruptive force. But amid the continuing fallout of the global opioid crisis, new technologies are being developed every day to limit and potentially even eliminate pain. Professor Hannah Fry learns about the future of pain management and how revolutionary technologies are being developed to directly control pain signals. She talks to the scientists behind these technologies about how this unprecedented breakthrough works, as well as meeting pain research participants themselves in order to understand the life-changing implications of such research. Along the way, she considers how society views pain and what a pain-free future would truly mean for humanity.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: The rollercoaster has been sending our hearts racing and stomachs dropping for over a century, and today, millions of us get our kicks on these topsy-turvy, daredevil joyriders. Hannah gets the inside story on the UK’s newest, tallest and fastest rollercoaster – Thorpe Park’s Hyperia. She uncovers the wild origins of the modern-day coaster and finds out how some dodgy French physics in the 19th century, Nasa rocket scientists and an ambitious cartoonist called Walt delivered the ultimate thrill machine.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Dean and Charlotte team up to restore a pair of motorcycle racing goggles with a rich history, Tim fixes a 1950s bike, and Will repairs a toy boat handmade by a devoted dad.

programme.title: Murder Case
programme.desc: When a family home in an affluent suburb of Glasgow is deliberately set on fire, detectives race to determine who attacked the young couple staying there, and why.

programme.title: QI
programme.desc: A selection of the best moments from series T, with Sandi Toksvig and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight

Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.
